local_help_spans.help_text: A second time: both visible instrumental singular forms in the complete hypothetical clause of44.7. The source headword sīð is not an instruction to leave the noun uninflected.

local_help_spans.phrase: ðæs gingstan / ðǣm ieldestan / ðone gingstan
local_help_spans.help_text: The youngest and eldest refer to individual brothers. Supply the masculine singular human referents and each case, rather than inferring substantive person uses from familiar adjective headwords.
A little earlier: lȳtle is instrumental of degree/difference with the comparative adverb ǣr. Cook’s original note points to178. It is not a feminine accusative object.

local_help_spans.phrase: twā hund punda goldes and fēower hund punda gewihte seolfres
local_help_spans.help_text: Two hundred pounds of gold and four hundred pounds by weight of silver. Hund means hundred, never dog here. Punda is genitive plural after the hundreds; goldes/seolfres are material genitives. The whole quantity frame remains visible; no new unaided numeral government is assumed.
The greatest part of costly clothing. Mǣstan is weak accusative masculine singular with dǣl; dēorwurðes agrees with the genitive neuter singular rēafes.

local_help_spans.phrase: twēntig ðēowa manna / tō ðǣm ðēowum mannum
local_help_spans.help_text: Twenty enslaved men; to the enslaved men. Keep original ðēowa without r. BT1053 supports the strong noun; BT1054’s adjective quotation actually has þeówra WITH r. The selected contextual strong-noun inference is bounded; no claim excludes every historical adjectival variant.

local_help_spans.phrase: ealle ðā męnn hiere giefa hęredon ðe hīe gesāwon
local_help_spans.help_text: All the men who saw them praised her gifts. The relative ðe is subject and reaches back to męnn; hīe is the accusative plural gifts. The relative clause is separated from its antecedent. Supply these reference links explicitly.
Wished them to be well: hīe refers to the king and princess and is the accusative actor of bēon; gesunde is accusative plural predicate. The complete construction is supplied.

May you be well: gē is nominative plural and gesunde nominative plural predicate. This is a direct wish with a plural subjunctive, distinct from the preceding accusative-infinitive construction despite identical gesunde.

Pitier of the poor / lover of learning. Supply both agent nouns and their object genitives. These phrases address the king and princess respectively; historical or Latin parallels in the original notes are explained in English.

local_help_spans.phrase: ðēowum mannum ðe ðæt mǣden him forgiefen hæfde
local_help_spans.help_text: The enslaved men whom the girl had given to him. Relative ðe is accusative plural; mǣden is the subject; him is Apollonius.
Said to them: him is dative plural referring to the servants; tō follows the verb while governing him.

local_help_spans.phrase: gān wē sēcean ūre giesthūs, ðæt wē mægen ūs geręstan
local_help_spans.help_text: Let us go seek our guesthouse, so that we may rest. Gān wē is hortative; ðæt marks purpose; ūs is accusative plural reflexive with geręstan. This completes the selected passage; the next teacher scene is outside its boundary.
My silver cup; the entire strong accusative adjective is supplied. Earlier proposed læfel seolfres is withdrawn because a direct material-genitive frame was not established by the checked evidence.
For your good / for your benefit. Ēowerre and ðearfe are dative feminine singular. Use the whole phrase visibly.
Because of that money / on account of that money. Ðǣm and fēo are dative neuter singular.
Above us all / more than all of us, describing the father’s preference. Ūs and ealle are accusative plural.
Outside the city. Byrig is dative singular. The preposition here gives a location, rather than the separate without/absence or unless uses.
